messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Re: SNP filtering
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

The issue seems to arise because your genlight object was created using dartR instead of dartRverse.

When you open your RStudio session with a genlight object created by dartR in your workspace/environment, RStudio automatically loads dartR, which overrides (or "masks") the functions from dartRverse. This means the functions you run will be from dartR, not dartRverse.

To resolve this issue, you can choose one of the following approaches:

Read your input file using dartRverse functions
Clear your workspace.
Restart R.
Load dartRverse and read your input file (e.g., DArT report or any other format) using dartRverse's dedicated reading functions: gl.read.csv, gl.read.dart, gl.read.fasta, gl.read.PLINK, gl.read.silicodart, or gl.read.vcf.

Change the class of your "genlight" object
Convert the class of your genlight object to be compatible with dartRverse as shown in the example code below:
Cheers,
Luis

library(dartRverse)
# load genlight object created using dartR
t1 <- gl.load("test.rds")
# assign the class "dartR" to genlight object
class(t1) <- "dartR"
# saving "dartR" object
gl.save(t1,"test2.rds")
# 1. Clean your workspace: Menu > Session > Clear Worspace
# 2. Restart R: Menu > Session > Restart R
# 3. Load dartRverse
library(dartRverse)
# load dartR object
t2 <- gl.load("test2.rds")
# convert to VCF
gl2vcf(t2,

       plink.bin.path = getwd(),
       outpath = getwd(),
       outfile = "test_vcf",

       snp.pos = "ChromPosTag_Rice_RGAP_v7",
       snp.chr = "Chrom_Rice_RGAP_v7")
# read VCF
t3 <- gl.read.vcf("test_vcf.vcf")

messages.subject: mutation rate per generation per base
messages.subject_clean: mutation rate per generation per base
messages.body_plain:
Hi dartR people,

I have dartseq SNP data from known parent-offspring. Is there a way to calculate mutation rate per site per generation?

Cheers
Kwan
messages.body_snippet:
Hi dartR people,

I have dartseq SNP data from known parent-offspring. Is there a way to calculate mutation rate per site per generation?

Cheers
Kwan

messages.subject: Re: mutation rate per generation per base
messages.subject_clean: mutation rate per generation per base
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kwan,

Estimating mutation rates using parents-offspring trios and DArTseq should be technically possible. DArTseq surveys 5-10% of the genome and typically there are around 1 to 50 de novo mutations in offsprings. It would be a matter of finding those SNPS in which both parents are homozygous for the same allele and the offspring is heterozygous. However, there are many other factors to take into account in the estimation of mutation rates, see for example a recent review from Bergeron, Lucie A., et al. "Evolution of the germline mutation rate across vertebrates." Nature 615.7951 (2023): 285-291.

Cheers,
Luis

messages.subject: gl.subsample.ind doesn't subsample metadata?
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I'm interested in calculating various genetic diversity metrics for my dataset of a threatened species - normally my sample sizes would be consistent across populations but because it's a threatened species, all population sizes are small and highly variable (range: 4-24 individuals).

I planned to even out the sample sizes for diversity calculations by using gl.subsample.ind to generate a gl object with all populations randomly subsampled to the lowest population size (ie. 4, or perhaps excluding the smallest pop and subsampling to the next smallest at 7). But I don't think I'm understanding the function because it only seems to subsample the individuals and loci but doesn't subsample the ind and loc metrics data along with them? All that comes up in the gl@other slot is $history. All the other ind and loc metrics are gone.

Have I done something wrong here? Is there a better way to randomly subsample populations to a specified sample size?

Cheers,
Rachel

messages.body_plain:
Hi Rachel,

To test the effect of five population sample sizes (n = 10, 5, 4, 3, 2) on observed heterozygosity estimates, the function gl.report.heterozygosity subsamples individuals, without replacement (see code below). The subsampling is repeated 10 times for each sample size n. This approach is an implementation of Schmidt et al (2021).

library(dartRverse)
t1 <- platypus.gl <http://platypus.gl>
res <- gl.report.heterozygosity(t1, subsample.pop = TRUE)

Schmidt, T. L., Jasper, M. E., Weeks, A. R., & Hoffmann, A. A. (2021). Unbiased population heterozygosity estimates from genome‐wide sequence data. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 12(10), 1888-1898.

Cheers,
Luis

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] gl.subsample.ind doesn't subsample metadata?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Guys,

Just a note that subsampling after SNPs are called does not resolve all the biases we found in our paper: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/1755-0998.13947

To do this, you have to actually call SNPs on the n target individuals for each of the 10 sets of individuals. Subsampling after you’ve already done SNP calling on a wider batch of individuals does not guarantee you fix the issues, and you can’t actually see whether you fixed them or not without re-calling your SNPs.

This will be especially problematic if you have reasons to suspect very big differences in underlying population diversity, such as one population has a much bigger or smaller population size.

Cheers,

Renee

Hi Luis and Renee, appreciate the speedy responses!

I'm not looking to test the effects of varied sample sizes, I just want to standardise all my populations to the same size, based on the smallest population that I have (or a nominated size threshold). I have already calculated autosomal heterozygosity in a similar process to the papers cited, I'm now looking for additional diversity parameters that are more sensitive to population size changes (my species is long lived and outcrossing so heterozygosity isn't telling me much). And I'm looking at parameters that are relative among populations, like % polymorphic loci, private alleles and allelic richness, so I need to use a single dataset with all the same snps called across populations. I'm now just wanting to standardise my population sizes and I thought that was the intention of the gl.subsample.ind function.

I can do the standardisation manually easily enough but is there a function already available that could automate that process?

Cheers,
Rachel

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] gl.subsample.ind doesn't subsample metadata?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rachel,

If you have already done autosomal heterozygosity through stacks or something, my recommendation is to standardise population sizes in your popmap and run gstacks/populations again. Then use the vcf file generated to do these analyses. It is the most theoretically robust way to do these analyses.

I can give you an r script to get from VCF to the gl with all the proper metadata and doing some of the really broad filtering. Send me an email.

Cheers,

Renee
